query: For high-entropy alloys intended for aerospace fasteners, what single intervention could improve the combination of mechanical durability, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence that supports it, and an experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Zirconium alloying of as‐cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni eutectic high-entropy alloys refines the microstructure by forming fine, stable Zr-rich precipitates that improve mechanical durability, suppress room-temperature creep, and enhance corrosion resistance compared to the unalloyed baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni eutectic high-entropy alloy, prepared without zirconium.
generation.intervention: Introduce zirconium (at a controlled alloying level, e.g., on the order of 1–3 wt%) into the alloy composition during casting.
generation.conditions: Aerospace fastener application conditions at room temperature, where mechanical loading, low-temperature creep, and corrosive environments (e.g., salt spray or humidity exposure) are relevant.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of fine, uniformly distributed Zr-rich precipitates and associated grain refinement.
generation.mechanism: Zirconium addition promotes the nucleation of stable, fine-scale precipitates that impede dislocation motion (enhancing mechanical durability), obstruct mechanisms of creep by pinning grain boundaries, and reduce intergranular susceptibility to corrosion by stabilizing grain boundary chemistry and structure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unalloyed baseline, the zirconium-alloyed high-entropy alloy is predicted to show improved mechanical strength and toughness, lower room-temperature creep rates, and reduced corrosion rates; the improvements should be simultaneously measurable under aerospace fastener service conditions.
generation.baseline: The as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni eutectic high-entropy alloy without zirconium addition.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected under room temperature and moderate environmental conditions typical for aerospace fasteners; the effects may not persist under extreme thermal cycling or highly aggressive chemical environments that exceed standard operational ranges.
generation.uncertainty: While qualitative improvements across multiple properties are anticipated, the exact quantitative magnitude of the improvements is uncertain and may require optimization of the zirconium content and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy specimens with varying levels of zirconium addition (including a zero-Zr control). Process all specimens under identical casting and thermal conditions. Subject them to standardized mechanical tests (e.g., tensile and impact testing), room-temperature creep experiments, and corrosion tests (e.g., salt spray or electrochemical corrosion measurements) representative of aerospace fastener conditions.
measurements: Mechanical durability: yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and toughness
Creep resistance: room-temperature creep strain rates under fixed load conditions
Corrosion resistance: corrosion rate measurements (e.g., weight loss, potential/current measurements)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If none of the zirconium-alloyed specimens demonstrate statistically significant (e.g., >10–15% improvement) simultaneous enhancements in mechanical durability, decreased creep rate, and improved corrosion resistance compared to the zero-Zr control, then the hypothesis is falsified.
